title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 6 Lesson 2: Two Connected Rough Systems custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two blocks $A$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_A = 0.2$) and $B$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_B = 0.3$) on a rough horizontal table are connected by a taut light string. A horizontal force $P$ pulls block $B$ away from $A$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the maximum value of $P$ for which the system remains in equilibrium, and the string tension $T$ at this instant.

Block $A$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_A = 0.3$) rests on a rough horizontal table. Block $B$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_B = 0.2$) rests on a rough $30^\circ$ incline. A light string connects $A$ and $B$ over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, explain why the system remains in equilibrium, and find the actual friction force on block $A$.

Two blocks $A$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_A = 0.2$) and $B$ of mass $m_B$ ($\mu_B = 0.25$) rest on opposite faces of a symmetrical wedge, both inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, connected by a light string over a smooth apex pulley. If block $A$ is in limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding down, calculate $m_B$ correct to 3 significant figures.

Two blocks $P$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_P = 0.1$) and $Q$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ ($\mu_Q = 0.6$) are connected by a taut light string on a slope inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal, with $P$ lower down the slope than $Q$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the friction force on block $P$ and the tension $T$ in the string in equilibrium.

Block $A$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ rests on top of block $B$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$, which rests on a rough horizontal table ($\mu_B = 0.2$). The coefficient of friction between $A$ and $B$ is $\mu_A = 0.4$. A horizontal force $P$ is applied to bottom block $B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the maximum force $P$ for which the entire system remains in static equilibrium without sliding.

A light string with uniform tension $T = 50\text{ N}$ passes over a smooth pulley at the apex of a wedge connecting two slopes inclined at $30^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. Both string segments run along the respective lines of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the angle between the two string segments and the magnitude of the resultant force $R_P$ on the pulley correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Block $A$ of mass $6\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal surface with $\mu_A = 0.4$. Block $B$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal with $\mu_B = 0.2$. A light inextensible string connects $A$ and $B$ over a smooth pulley at the edge. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum friction force on each block, and determine the tension $T$ in the string when block $B$ is in limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding down the slope.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why block $A$ does not move, and state the actual magnitude and direction of the friction force acting on block $A$.

questions.prompt: Block $A$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$ and block $B$ of mass $6\text{ kg}$ are connected by a taut light horizontal string on a rough horizontal floor, with $\mu_A = 0.25$ and $\mu_B = 0.35$. A horizontal force $P$ pulls block $B$ to the right away from block $A$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum possible friction forces $F_{A,\max}$ and $F_{B,\max}$ that can act on each block.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum value of $P$ for which the system remains in equilibrium, and find the tension $T$ in the connecting string at this instant.

questions.prompt: A fixed wedge has two rough faces inclined at $30^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. Block $A$ of mass $m_A = 4\text{ kg}$ rests on the $30^\circ$ face ($\mu_A = 0.3$). Block $B$ of mass $m_B$ rests on the $45^\circ$ face ($\mu_B = 0.2$). The blocks are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the apex. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If block $A$ is in limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding down its $30^\circ$ face, calculate the string tension $T$ and the mass $m_B$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If instead block $B$ is on the point of sliding down its $45^\circ$ face, calculate the new mass $m_B'$ of the block, and state the range of values of $m_B$ for equilibrium.

questions.prompt: Two blocks $P$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ and $Q$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light rigid rod and placed on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, with $P$ positioned higher up the plane than $Q$. The coefficients of friction are $\mu_P = 0.4$ and $\mu_Q = 0.1$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the blocks cannot remain in equilibrium without external support, and calculate the minimum holding force $F_{\text{hold}}$ parallel to the slope needed to prevent sliding correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If this minimum holding force of $25.3\text{ N}$ is applied entirely to lower block $Q$ directed up the slope, determine the thrust (compressive force) in the connecting rod correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Block $A$ of mass $8\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal table ($\mu_A = 0.25$). Block $B$ of mass $12\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal ($\mu_B = 0.3$). The blocks are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table. A horizontal force of magnitude $P$ is applied to block $A$ directed away from the pulley. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum friction forces $F_{A,\max}$ and $F_{B,\max}$ on both blocks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When block $B$ is on the point of sliding down the incline, calculate the minimum force $P_{\min}$ needed to maintain equilibrium correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum force $P_{\max}$ before block $A$ starts sliding away from the pulley (dragging block $B$ up the slope), and state the range of values of $P$ for equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A fixed symmetrical wedge has two faces inclined at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. Block $A$ of mass $m$ rests on the left face with $\mu_A = 0.5$, and block $B$ of mass $2m$ rests on the right face with $\mu_B = 0.2$. The blocks are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the apex. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the system is in limiting equilibrium with block $B$ on the verge of sliding down its face, find the exact value of $\tan\theta$ and calculate $\theta$ in degrees correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the wedge angle is decreased to $\theta = 30^\circ$, explain why the system remains in static equilibrium, and calculate the string tension $T$ when block $B$ reaches limiting equilibrium in terms of $mg$.

questions.prompt: Block $B$ of mass $m_B = 6\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction $\mu_2 = 0.3$ between $B$ and the plane. A smaller block $A$ of mass $m_A = 2\text{ kg}$ rests on top of block $B$, with coefficient of friction $\mu_1 = 0.4$ between $A$ and $B$. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth fixed pulley at the top of the incline and connects to block $B$, with both string segments parallel to the slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction $R_1$ between $A$ and $B$, the normal reaction $R_2$ between $B$ and the plane, and the maximum static friction forces $F_{1,\max}$ and $F_{2,\max}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If block $B$ is on the point of sliding down the incline (which pulls block $A$ up the incline), formulate the equilibrium equation for block $A$ and calculate the tension $T$ in the string correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the force $P$ directed down the plane that must be applied to block $B$ to produce this limiting downward motion, and explain why the system remains at rest under gravity alone without $P$.
